Alias sources

Each RadioReference system you load (Playlists → Load) and each CSV you import is kept here and merged; the newest source wins when two name the same talkgroup. Priority, alert, avoid and lock-out are your own settings and apply whichever source names the talkgroup — the same model as SDRTrunk's alias lists.

Talkgroup ranges

A rule covers every talkgroup in the range — the way SDRTrunk alias ranges and OP25 whitelists work. Explicit per-talkgroup settings win over a range; the engine applies lock-out and priority ranges natively.

Alerts
No alerts yet. An alert watches talkgroups for keywords in the transcript (or an emergency, any call, or a radio) and sends a Telegram message with the audio.
Edit alert

Keyword alerts fire when the transcript arrives, so they trail the call by the transcription time. The cooldown keeps one incident from sending a message per transmission.

Conversations · summarise the back-and-forth
A rule watches talkgroups where one party is fixed (a hospital) and mobile units call in. Each back-and-forth becomes one incident: when it goes quiet the transcripts are stitched, the local model summarises them, and the summary goes to Telegram with the combined audio. A late transmission revises it (old message deleted, new one sent).
Edit conversation rule

Needs transcription on (Settings) and an Ollama model chosen above. The summary waits up to 90 s past the quiet gap for transcripts to land.

Telegram

No radio detected. Plug in an Airspy or RTL-SDR and press Rescan.

The top-bar Radio picker lists these. On start-up the app picks the saved radio if it is attached, otherwise the first Airspy, otherwise the first RTL-SDR.

Band coverage · the other radios

The radio picked in the top bar holds the control channel. Every other attached radio marked cover is parked on a part of the site's span the primary cannot see, so calls granted there are decoded too — the way Unitrunker spreads a site over several tuners.

Radio

Gain and frequency correction are per radio, in the Devices tab. Radio and sample rate are in the top bar. Airspy at 10 M covers a whole site (±3.84 MHz); 2.5 M covers ±0.96 MHz; RTL-SDR covers ±1.2 MHz. The follower measures and compensates tuner error on its own; the ppm value keeps the radio centred where the band centre says, which matters at the band edges.

Library
—
Audio & recording

WAV is always captured first; other formats are made by ffmpeg and replace it. Speech at 8 kHz sounds fine at 24–32 kbit/s.

Per-talkgroup exceptions are set in the Aliases tab (Rec · Str · Up). A call that is not recorded still appears in the call history and library, without audio.

Share calls · rdio-scanner / OpenMHz / Broadcastify Calls

Each call is sent once per service after it completes (WAV to rdio-scanner; M4A/MP3 via ffmpeg to OpenMHz and Broadcastify). Outcomes are kept per call; re-send from a call's detail in the Library.

Script hook · run a program after each call

The call arrives as environment variables — HS_TG, HS_TG_NAME, HS_UNIT, HS_UNIT_NAME, HS_FREQ_HZ, HS_SECS, HS_EMERGENCY, HS_AUDIO, HS_JSON, HS_SYSTEM, HS_TALKER_ALIAS — and as one JSON object on standard input. Runs off the decode thread, one at a time.

Live feed · Icecast / Broadcastify

Broadcastify feeds: use the host, port, mount and source password from your feed's "Feed Technical Details" page. Encoding and connection are done by ffmpeg.

RadioReference account
Premium account required. Secrets are kept in the Keychain on this Mac.

Decodes unencrypted P25 only. Encrypted talkgroups are detected by ALGID and skipped by architecture — never decrypted. In Indiana, use at your own dwelling or place of business (IC 35-44.1-2-7).
